chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: First hearing Big Sid Catlett in Milwaukee
summary: In 1931 Catlett filled in for the sick Cuba Austin with McKinney's band and made everyone forget him.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And now, Big Sid, Big Sid Catlett, when I first worked with him was with McKinney's band, and he come in and took Cuba's place and, gee whiz, he almost made us forget about Cuba, --
-- because he could do anything Cuba could do, only he did it with more finesse, --
-- you see. And just as a kid Big Sid was a fantastic drummer. And he -- Of course, when I left McKinney's band after --
You mentioned that he came in one time and played in --
In Cuba's place. When we played a dance up in Milwaukee, Cuba got sick in Chicago and, of course,
you know Big Sidney Catlett was from Chicago.
Well, we picked him up to take us up to the Eagle Ballroom in Milwaukee to play.
About what year was that about?
1931. That was before Don left McKinney's band to get his own band.
That's about the first time you heard Big Sid?
First time I heard him and I never forgot him after that and nobody in the band did either.
And that was even before that he had left with -- the next time I heard of him, well, he was with Sam Wooding. You see, that was the next time I heard of Big Sid.
